releases.title: IMDA and NUH Partner in First Open Innovation Platform Collaboration in Public Healthcare
releases.body:
Partnership accelerates healthcare innovation by connecting real-world hospital needs with technology expertise

SINGAPORE, Oct. 28, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) and the National University Hospital (NUH), through its Kent Ridge Office of Innovation (KROI), have signed a Memorandum of Intent (MOI), marking IMDA's first Open Innovation Platform (OIP) partnership with a public healthcare institution. The partnership aims to accelerate healthcare innovation by connecting real-world challenges faced by healthcare professionals with technology innovators who can develop and test practical solutions.

Established in April 2024, KROI works closely with clinical and operational teams across NUH to identify areas where innovation can enhance care delivery, patient experience and operational efficiency. This partnership brings together NUH's clinical and operational expertise with IMDA's OIP network of approximately 21,000 innovators and solution providers, including startups, technology firms, and research institutions. It also supports Singapore's National AI Strategy (NAIS) to drive AI innovation and adoption in key sectors such as healthcare.

Turning healthcare challenges into practical solutions

By focusing on needs identified by healthcare professionals rather than technology alone, NUH can tap on the expertise across the OIP network to identify, evaluate and pilot promising solutions that address its priority healthcare challenges and make a meaningful difference to patients and healthcare staff in a real-world hospital setting. The MOI has already seen the launch of its first healthcare-themed innovation challenge seeking AI-enabled solutions to help identify fall hazards in patients' homes earlier and at scale, with Calls for Applications (CFAs) closing in November 2026.

Since its launch in 2018, IMDA's OIP has facilitated more than 450 innovation challenges and supported over S$25 million in prize funding, helping organisations tap external technology expertise to address business and operational needs.

Dr Ling Zheng Jye, Head of the Kent Ridge Office of Innovation, said: "Healthcare innovation is most impactful when it addresses real needs on the ground. Through the Open Innovation Platform, we can engage a broad community of innovators to tackle challenges identified by our clinicians and operational teams, creating new opportunities to develop and test solutions that can benefit both patients and healthcare professionals."

Mr. Alvin Kang, Director of Innovation at IMDA, said: "In support of Singapore's National AI Strategy, we are bringing IMDA's open innovation capabilities into healthcare, and creating opportunities for technology companies to apply their expertise to real clinical and operational challenges. By working with NUH through our Open Innovation Platform, we want to help turn promising innovations into practical solutions that can improve healthcare delivery."

A foundation for future collaboration

The IMDA-NUH partnership builds on KROI's broader efforts to strengthen ties across Singapore's innovation ecosystem. These include collaborations with organisations such as the National University of Singapore and academic publisher Elsevier, as well as the launch of the NUH Innovation Hub earlier this year, which supports the development, evaluation and implementation of staff-led innovations, including MedBot, NUH's AI-powered virtual pharmacy assistant.

Building on this momentum, NUH plans to launch innovation challenges on IMDA's OIP in March, July and October each year. These regular challenge calls will provide opportunities for technology innovators to develop and pilot solutions in response to priority areas identified by the hospital, thereby creating additional avenues for collaboration between healthcare providers and industry.

About Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA)

The Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) leads Singapore's digital transformation by developing a vibrant digital economy and an inclusive digital society. As Architects of Singapore's Digital Future, we foster growth in Infocomm Technology and Media sectors in concert with progressive regulations, harnessing frontier technologies, and developing local talent and digital infrastructure ecosystems to establish Singapore as a digital metropolis.

For more news and information, visit www.imda.gov.sg or follow IMDA on LinkedIn (IMDAsg), Facebook (IMDAsg) and Instagram (@imdasg).

About the National University Hospital (NUH)

The National University Hospital (NUH) is Singapore's university hospital. While the hospital at Kent Ridge first received its patients on 24 June 1985, our legacy started from 1905, the date of the founding of what is today the NUS Yong Loo Lin School of Medicine. NUH is the principal teaching hospital of the medical school.

Our unique identity as a university hospital is a key attraction for healthcare professionals who aspire to do more than practise tertiary medical care. We offer an environment where research and teaching are an integral part of medicine, and continue to shape medicine and transform care for the community we care for.

We are an academic medical centre with over 1,200 beds, serving more than one million patients a year with over 50 medical, surgical and dental specialties. NUH is the only public and not-for-profit hospital in Singapore to provide trusted care for adults, women and children under one roof, including the only paediatric kidney and liver transplant programme in the country.

The NUH is a key member of the National University Health System (NUHS), one of three public healthcare clusters in Singapore. For more information, visit www.nuh.com.sg

releases.title: World's Largest Flying Digital Screen Makes NYC Debut with Two Flights and New Byron Allen Media Partnership
releases.body:
HELI-D flew over the Hudson River near Chelsea Piers and the Statue of Liberty during the DPAA Global Video Everywhere Summit, followed by an evening flight showcasing Byron Allen's media content

NEW YORK, Oct. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- HELI-D, the company behind the world's largest flying digital screen, made its New York City debut on October 13 with two flights introducing a new form of aerial digital advertising to one of the world's largest media markets. The debut featured an afternoon flight in partnership with the Digital Place Based Advertising Association (DPAA) during its annual Global Video Everywhere Summit, followed by an evening flight showcasing content from media mogul Byron Allen's Allen Media Group as part of a newly secured partnership.

The afternoon flight took place between 1:00 PM and 1:45 PM ET, coinciding with the Summit's lunch break. Launching from Newport Helistop in New Jersey, HELI-D flew along the Hudson River toward Chelsea Piers, where Summit attendees and New Yorkers had an opportunity to see the massive digital screen in action. The aircraft then headed south toward the Statue of Liberty, bringing the display to one of the city's most recognizable landmarks.

HELI-D returned to the skies later that evening for a second flight featuring content from Byron Allen's Allen Media Group. The new agreement marks a significant step in HELI-D's entry into the U.S. advertising market, bringing together its aerial digital display technology and one of the country's prominent media entrepreneurs.

Unlike traditional billboards fixed to buildings or roadside structures, HELI-D's technology takes digital out-of-home advertising into the sky, creating a mobile, large-scale display capable of bringing brand messages directly to high-visibility locations, major events and large audiences.

"New York City is one of the most important advertising markets in the world, and there's no better place to demonstrate what's possible when digital advertising takes to the skies," said Simon Powell, Co-Founder and CEO of HELI-D. "Launching with DPAA and The Ad Council, and now working with Byron Allen and his media company, makes this an incredibly exciting debut for us. These partnerships demonstrate the potential of our technology to bring major brands and media content to audiences in an entirely new way."

The New York debut coincided with the DPAA Global Video Everywhere Summit, which brought together leaders from across the advertising, media and digital out-of-home industries. As a new media partner of DPAA and The Ad Council, HELI-D featured content from both organizations during the afternoon flight, demonstrating how its aerial display can be used for commercial advertising, public awareness campaigns and large-scale brand activations.

With two flights marking its New York City debut and new partnerships spanning the advertising and media industries, HELI-D is positioning its technology as a new addition to the digital out-of-home advertising landscape, offering brands the ability to deliver dynamic content above some of the world's most recognizable destinations and major events.

About HELI-D

HELI-D is a global leader in aerial digital media, redefining out-of-home advertising through high-impact, data-driven activations in the sky. Combining advanced aviation engineering with the world's brightest LED display systems, HELI-D transforms airspace into a programmable, measurable communications platform. With operations spanning UAE, Australia, and now the United States, the company partners with major brands, including Microsoft, TAB, and Netflix, to deliver record-setting campaigns that turn attention into action. HELI-D maintains a perfect safety record and offsets ten times its operational carbon emissions through verified sustainability programs.

About Remarkable Media Group

Remarkable Media Group is a global experiential media innovator, specializing in aerial advertising, immersive brand activations and next-level outdoor experiences. With operations across multiple continents, the company transforms sky and space into impactful platforms. From ultra-large-format helicopter-towed banners, drone-banner fleets and sky-typing messages, to night-time video helicopter banners and parachute-deployed product sampling. Whether creating world-first aerial installations or record-breaking brand moments, Remarkable Media Group partners with agencies and forward-thinking brands to amplify impact, tell bold stories and capture attention in the world's most visible skies. To learn more, visit www.remarkablemedia.com

releases.title: Mersive Collaboration Suite Is Now Mersive Polaris
releases.body:
New name retires the Gen 4 and MCS labels to better reflect where Mersive is steering collaboration next.

DENVER, Oct. 8, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Mersive Technologies today announced that its collaboration platform, previously known as Gen 4 and the Mersive Collaboration Suite (MCS), is now Mersive Polaris. Its website and visual identity have been updated to match.

Mersive Solstice defined its category, showing that a room could share wirelessly, simply and reliably. But what rooms are asked to do has changed. Meetings now span more platforms, more networks and more devices than any one room was designed for.

Answering that took more than new hardware. Drawing on fourteen years of deployments and feedback from IT and AV teams, Mersive rebuilt the platform with software at its core, so rooms keep improving long after install day.

"Gen 4" made that sound like the next step in a hardware sequence. It isn't. It's built for the landscape rooms work in now, and it needed its own name.

Every generation of this line has looked up: Mersive Sol in 2012, then Solstice Gen 1 in 2013, Gen 2 in 2015, Gen 2i in 2017 and Gen 3 in 2019. While a solstice marks a turning point, Polaris is the fixed point the northern sky turns around, the star navigators steer by, and the role Mersive intends to play in customers' spaces for the next decade.

"Solstice showed the market what wireless collaboration could be," said Damian Blazy, CEO of Mersive. "Calling what came next a fourth generation undersold it."

"Polaris isn't the next Solstice with a new label," said Ryan Lee, Vice President of Product at Mersive. "It's a different way of building, and the name signals that."

Mersive Polaris includes Polaris Essentials, Polaris Pro and Polaris Host. Gen 4 and MCS customers are using the same products, now under the Polaris name.

Solstice Gen 3 is supported into 2029, with a mapped transition path and a trade-in program. It runs side by side with Polaris, so customers can upgrade room by room at their own pace.

To learn more, visit the Mersive website.

Media Contact

Skyler Bowden, sbowden@mersive.com

About Mersive Technologies

Mersive Technologies helps people connect and collaborate in meeting rooms, huddle spaces and classrooms. Today's meetings span more platforms, networks and devices than any one room was designed for, with people joining from anywhere. Mersive Polaris, the successor to its Solstice line, was built for that hybrid reality. With software at its core, Polaris lets anyone in the room share content wirelessly from their own device and connect with remote participants on any conferencing platform. Rooms keep improving long after install day, and IT teams can centrally manage, monitor and update deployments of any size. Mersive is headquartered in Lakewood, Colorado. To learn more, visit www.mersive.com.
